subject: Follow-up: ACME Health capacity commitments + POC test matrix
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Emma Walsh <emma.walsh@acme-health.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: ACME Health capacity commitments + POC test matrix

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track: 

Summary from call:
- Primary goal: validate predictable inference throughput for ACME's claims-extraction workload (avg doc length ~1.8k tokens, 95th p95 latency target ~250ms).
- Key constraint: capacity guarantees for peak reporting windows (Mon 8–10am ET) and ability to burst to cloud for seasonal spikes.
- ACME will evaluate cost/SLA tradeoffs between Reserved GPUs on Hyperscaler vs Redwood Dedicated.

Proposed next steps (suggested owners & timeline):
1) POC kickoff (scope + test matrix) — Redwood to propose concrete test matrix by Thu, Feb 5 (owner: me / Karthik).
2) Capacity commitments doc — ACME to share expected concurrency and weekly consumption windows (owner: Emma / cloudinfra@acme-health.com) by Fri, Feb 6.
3) Benchmark run — redwood to run three scenarios: baseline: dev single-instance; production: dedicated reserved pool; fallback: hyperscaler burst. We’ll provide cost and p95 latency per scenario. (owner: Redwood infra)
4) Security & procurement — share any outstanding questionnaire items; if NDA is needed, we can circulate (owner: ACME legal).

Attached: acme-poc-scope-v1.pdf (first draft scope), I also attached a lightweight checklist we’ll iterate on.

Questions for you now:
- Can you confirm the expected peak concurrent requests/hour and typical token distribution for the claims documents?
- Any procurement timelines we should be aware of (SOW/PO cadence)?

If this looks good I’ll push a versioned test matrix (concrete config: instance types, model sizes, sequence length, batching settings) and schedule a technical kickoff next week.

Best,
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Thanks Jasmine — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Peak concurrency: our internal dashboard shows 180–220 concurrent inference requests during peak reporting windows, with spikes up to ~300 for short bursts (10–15 minutes).
- Token distribution: median ~900 tokens, 95th ~2,100 tokens.
- Procurement: we target a decision window by end of March; procurement wants a clear SLO and an option for a 6–12 month reserved capacity contract.

We’re happy to run the NDA if that helps move faster — I’ll attach the standard ACME NDA template to my next message. Also looping in cloudinfra to confirm they can share any additional telemetry.

–Emma

Subject: RE: Follow-up: ACME Health capacity commitments + POC test matrix

Emma / team —

Thanks for the numbers, that’s very helpful. I put together a first-pass test matrix and recommended configs — attaching redwood-vs-hyperscaler-test-matrix.xlsx. High-level notes: 

Test matrix highlights (short):
- Workloads: interactive (single-request latency), batch (throughput for nightly reconciliation), heavy-burst (short-duration spikes).
- Redwood Dedicated config: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved pool), autoscale cushion + burst policy to 6 GPUs for 15 minutes; KV cache enabled for common prefixes; optimized kernel path for 2k token context. Expected 95th latency ~190–260ms depending on batching.
- Hyperscaler reserved config: 3–4 reserved instances across zones; longer cold-starts for model caching and higher per-token cost; burstable to additional instances but with less predictable latency during cache warm-up.
- Acceptance criteria: p95 latency <= 250ms for interactive; throughput targets for nightly jobs within 10% of baseline.

Questions for ACME infra: can you share whether you require single-tenant physical isolation or whether tenant-level dedicated pools with network isolation suffice? That will materially change the procurement contract and pricing.

Proposed immediate deliverables:
1) Redwood: run quick synthetic runs on representative payloads (we’ll mirror ACME token distribution) and share results by Tue, Feb 10.
2) ACME: confirm isolation requirement + return signed NDA if needed.
3) Joint: schedule a 60-minute technical POC kickoff week of Feb 16.

Attaching matrix now.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Solution Architecture, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-test-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB)
From: Emma Walsh <emma.walsh@acme-health.com>

Cc: cloudinfra@acme-health.com
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 11:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up: ACME Health capacity commitments + POC test matrix

Thanks Karthik — matrix looks good. Quick updates from our side: 

- We can accept tenant-level dedicated pools with strict network segmentation (no shared volume mounts); single-tenant hardware is not required at this stage.
- Procurement has reviewed timelines and asked for a sample SOW and a non-binding reserved capacity quote for 6 months.
- NDA: attaching signed copy (acme-nda-signed.pdf).

We’re happy to lock the Feb 17 POC kickoff at 11am ET — please send a calendar invite and the agenda. Also Emma from Hyperscaler sales copied earlier asked whether we’ll be sharing the test matrix; we’re Ok with sharing a trimmed version but will not share internal telemetry.

Looking forward — Emma
